points.description: Role of the learning rate: it controls the speed of convergence of steepest descent. A low learning rate gives slow, overdamped convergence, and a high learning rate gives underdamped convergence with a zigzagging path.
points.partial_credit: Half for saying only that the learning rate sets the speed, or only one of the low/high behaviours, without the overdamped or zigzag description.

points.description: Danger: when the learning rate exceeds a critical value, learning becomes unstable (the descent diverges or oscillates out of control rather than converging).
points.partial_credit: Half for saying only that a large learning rate is 'bad' or 'causes problems' without stating instability or divergence.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both parts: the learning rate sets the speed of convergence (slow and overdamped when low, underdamped and zigzagging when high), and the danger is instability once the learning rate exceeds a critical value. Half marks go to a right idea stated vaguely, such as "too high is bad" or only one of the low/high behaviours. Wrong or missing content on a part earns nothing for that part only.
